questions.q: Task: a speech to your class about banning phones at lunch. Which opening fits best?
options: Good morning, everyone. Should our school really ban phones at lunch?
Text A and Text B are both about phones.
questions.why: A speech addresses its audience directly; a rhetorical question engages listeners.

questions.q: Where should your overall position first be made clear in directed writing?
questions.why: State your position at the start, build the argument, and confirm it in a clear final judgement.

questions.q: What should you do in the last 10 minutes of the hour?
options: Reread both texts from the start
Check both texts are used, evaluation, register and accuracy
questions.why: Proofreading protects the 25 writing marks, where accuracy counts.

questions.q: What two things do the bullet points in the directed writing task require?
questions.model: Evaluate the ideas and opinions in both texts, and give your own views based on what you have read.
points: give your own views based on the texts
